alfred.intro: Alfred Bernhard Nobel held 355 patents, built an industrial empire across Europe, wrote poetry and drama — and used his fortune to create the world's most prestigious award.

business.text: Nobel built factories and laboratories in more than 20 countries, amassing one of the great fortunes of the 19th century. He was fluent in five languages and ran his empire largely by correspondence.
business.title: International businessman

early.text: Born in Stockholm in 1833, Alfred was the third son of engineer Immanuel Nobel. The family moved to Russia, where Alfred studied chemistry and engineering under renowned scientists in Saint Petersburg, Paris and the United States.
early.title: Early life

inventor.text: Nobel's great breakthrough was taming nitroglycerin. After years of dangerous experiments — his younger brother Emil died in an explosion in 1864 — he invented dynamite in 1867 and later gelignite and ballistite, transforming mining, construction and warfare.
inventor.title: Inventor and engineer

legacy.text: Today the Nobel Prize is the most prestigious award in science, literature and peacemaking — a legacy its founder, often called the 'merchant of death' in his lifetime, could hardly have imagined.
legacy.title: Legacy

personal.text: Behind the industrialist was a melancholic intellectual: he wrote poetry and plays, amassed a large library, and corresponded with leading thinkers of his age. He never married and had no children.
personal.title: The private Nobel

will.text: In 1895, a year before his death, Nobel signed the will dedicating his fortune to prizes for those who 'conferred the greatest benefit to humankind'. His family contested it, but the will prevailed — and the first prizes were awarded in 1901.
will.title: The final will

alfred.subtitle: 1833 – 1896 · Inventor, engineer, industrialist — founder of the Nobel Prize
alfred.title: Alfred Nobel

history.intro: In 1895, Alfred Nobel — inventor, engineer and industrialist — signed a will that would create the most famous prize in the world. Since 1901, the Nobel Prizes have honored those who conferred the greatest benefit to humankind.

ceremonies.text: Following Nobel's will, the prizes are awarded in Stockholm, Sweden — except the Peace Prize, which is awarded in Oslo, Norway, by a committee chosen by the Norwegian parliament. The ceremonies take place every December 10.
ceremonies.title: Stockholm and Oslo

economics.text: In 1968, Sweden's central bank (Sveriges Riksbank) established the Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel. First awarded in 1969, it is presented alongside the original five prizes.
economics.title: A sixth prize

first.text: On December 10, 1901 — the fifth anniversary of Nobel's death — the first Nobel Prizes were awarded. Among the inaugural laureates were Wilhelm Röntgen (Physics), Jacobus van 't Hoff (Chemistry) and Sully Prudhomme (Literature).
first.title: The first prizes — 1901

medal.text: Laureates receive a gold medal, a diploma and a monetary award. The medal bears Nobel's portrait with the inscription of his name; each diploma is a unique work of art. The prize amount has grown from 150,782 SEK in 1901 to over 10 million SEK today.
medal.title: Medals, diplomas and prize money

nobel.text: Born in Stockholm in 1833, Alfred Nobel was a chemist, engineer and inventor who held 355 patents. His fortune came largely from explosives — including dynamite, patented in 1867 — and from an international industrial empire spanning Europe.
nobel.title: Alfred Nobel

will.text: When Nobel died in 1896, his last will stunned his family: the bulk of his fortune was to fund annual prizes for physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, literature and peace. The will was contested, but in 1900 the Nobel Foundation was created to carry it out.
will.title: The will that shocked the world

sources.independence: Nobel Explorer is an independent educational project and is not affiliated with the Nobel Foundation, the Nobel Prize awarding institutions, or the Wikimedia Foundation.
sources.intro: Nobel Explorer is a lightweight discovery layer, not an encyclopedia. It keeps only a compact index of laureates — names, years, categories, motivations and topics — and loads biographies on demand from Wikipedia and Wikimedia.

points.text: Laureate names, award years, categories and motivations come from the official Nobel Prize API (api.nobelprize.org), which publishes its data openly.
points.title: Prize data

points.text: Biographical articles, extracts and portraits are retrieved live from Wikipedia / Wikimedia via the public MediaWiki APIs, and remain subject to Wikimedia licenses (CC BY-SA).
points.title: Biographies

points.text: Portrait thumbnails come from Wikimedia Commons through the Wikipedia API. Nobel Explorer hotlinks them with attribution rather than redistributing them.
points.title: Images

points.text: Only the compact laureate index ships with the app. Recently viewed laureates, language preference and a 24-hour Wikipedia cache live only in your browser — nothing is sent to our servers.
points.title: What we store
